headline.purpose: The current question heading and the intro heading; 20px at <=820px. The largest text in the app.

answer.purpose: Answer text in the reading column; 16.5px in the intro example, 16px at <=820px.

lede.purpose: The intro paragraph in Soft Ink, max 64ch.

refusal.purpose: The calm 'not in your documents' reply, in Soft Ink.

excerpt.purpose: Text quoted from a document inside an opened source row. The only serif use.

wordmark.purpose: 'Highwatch RAG' beside the logo in the top bar.

body.purpose: Base text with tabular numerals: source rows, notices, toasts.

label.purpose: Button labels, link buttons, the drop-zone instruction.

meta.purpose: Counts, hints, library notes, the budget line, the remove-confirmation line.

meta-sm.purpose: The document details line in the library.

tag.purpose: The Example tag on the intro card.

chip.purpose: Citation numerals in answers and the library.

chip-source.purpose: Citation numerals in the sources list.

shadows.name: composer-lift
shadows.purpose: The composer field at rest; replaced by the focus wash ring on focus.

shadows.name: button-contact
shadows.purpose: Secondary buttons at rest; removed when disabled.

shadows.name: focus-wash-ring
shadows.purpose: Composer field focus-within and the API-key input focus, with an Action Blue border. Elsewhere focus is a 2px Action Blue outline offset 2px.

shadows.name: lit-chip-ring
shadows.purpose: A citation chip that is hovered or lit, in the answer, the sources list or the library.

shadows.name: lit-mark-ring
shadows.purpose: A lit highlight mark grows 2px of its own ink (--c) and takes a faint ink rim.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Easing for the highlight swipe, the toast rise and the pending sweep.

motion.name: highlight-swipe
motion.value: background-size 0% 100% -> 100% 100%, 520ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), delay 120ms + 140ms x mark index
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: highlight inks grow left to right, in reading order, when an answer lands (and once on the intro example at load). The class is removed after 800ms + 140ms x mark count. Off under prefers-reduced-motion: marks show at rest.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Functional colour, border, opacity and ring transitions on controls, rows and chips.

motion.name: chevron-flip
motion.purpose: Source-row chevron when a source opens.

motion.name: spin
motion.value: rotate 360deg linear infinite; 900ms (Drive sync icon), 1.1s (working upload, processing document)

motion.name: pending-sweep
motion.purpose: The Highlighter Yellow segment inside the 96px searching bar.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; transition: none; scroll-behavior: auto }
motion.purpose: Everything stops; highlights appear at rest and smooth scrolling becomes instant.

breakpoints.name: narrow-desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Library narrows to 272px; in source rows the file name stacks above its location (13px).

breakpoints.name: single-column
breakpoints.purpose: Questions first: sticky top bar, thread, sticky composer, then the library. Page scrolls; model pill shows provider only; Enter hint hidden; question 20px, answer 16px; source rows wrap; toast full width 96px up; remove icon always visible.

breakpoints.name: no-hover
breakpoints.purpose: Remove icon always visible on document rows.

narrative.overview:
Highwatch RAG looks like a clean, familiar document tool: a white page, a grey library down the left, a centred reading column, and a question box pinned at the bottom. Its personality lives in one device. Every claim in an answer is marked with a highlighter ink, and that ink belongs to the source the claim came from: the same colour sits on the claim's number, on the source row, on the matched phrase inside the quoted excerpt, and on the document in the library. A reviewer can trace any sentence to its evidence by colour alone.

Everything else stays quiet so the inks can do that work. Neutrals are cool greys on white, separated by 1px hairlines and a change of tone rather than by stacked cards; one action blue carries the primary button, links and focus; type is one humanist sans with a book serif kept for text quoted from documents. Density is that of a desktop productivity app: 14px base text, 13px controls, and a 720px reading column with 17px answer text.

This world replaced an earlier themed direction (map rulers, survey-sheet page strips, a woodland rail) that the user rejected as dull, odd, and wrong in colour and type, and asked instead for "clean and premium: a familiar app layout, very polished, personality in the details". It wears no costume: no textures, motifs or decorative colour, and no dark chat-bubble template. An answer reads as document text under its question heading, not as a message.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, a cool grey library panel, 1px hairlines; flat except for the composer and the toast.
Five pale highlighter inks used only to mark evidence; citation n wears the same ink everywhere it appears.
Source Sans 3 for all UI and answers; Source Serif 4 only for quoted excerpts.
One action blue for the Ask button, links, drag-over and focus.
Irregular marker-tip corners on evidence (chips and highlight marks); regular 4–12px corners on everything else.
One authored motion: highlights swipe in, left to right, when an answer lands.

rules.name: The Evidence Ink Rule
rules.body: The highlighter inks mean "this came from a source". They appear only on evidence: highlight marks in answers, citation chips (in the answer, the sources list and the library) and the matched phrase in an excerpt. The only other yellow is the highlighter itself, drawn in the logo mark and in the sweep of the searching bar. Status, hover, selection, buttons and decoration never use an ink.

rules.name: The Same Colour Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Citation n wears ink ((n − 1) % 5) + 1 in every place it appears: its claim, its number, its source row, its excerpt phrase and its document's chip in the library. The ink comes from the number, never from position, file or relevance.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Action blue is the only interactive colour, and the Ask button is the only solid blue fill on screen. Secondary actions are white buttons with a Strong Hairline border.

rules.name: The Serif Means Quoted Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 is used only for text quoted from a document. Never for headings, answers, labels or UI.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: The whole app sets tabular numerals, so relevance scores, counts and citation numbers line up.

rules.name: The Questions First Rule
rules.body: At ≤820px the order is top bar, thread, composer, library: a reviewer can read the example and ask before scrolling past the upload controls.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: The thread and the composer share the same centred 720px column; nothing in the work area breaks out of it.

rules.name: The Two Lifts Rule
rules.body: Only the composer and the toast float. Every other surface sits flat on hairlines; a new panel or card gets a 1px Hairline border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Marker Tip Rule
rules.body: Irregular corners belong to evidence only (chips and highlight marks). Controls, cards and inputs keep regular radii, and chips never take a regular radius.

rules.name: The Shared Phrase Rule
rules.body: A highlight starts at the first word of the longest phrase (three or more words) the claim shares with its source and runs through its citation chip; the excerpt marks only that shared phrase, in the same ink. With no shared phrase, the whole claim is marked.

rules.name: The One Swipe Rule
rules.body: The highlight swipe is the only authored motion. Nothing else slides, fades in or staggers; everything else is instant or a short functional transition.

dos: **Do** derive a citation's ink from its number, ((n − 1) % 5) + 1, and repeat that ink on its claim, chip, source row, excerpt phrase and library chip.

**Do** start a highlight at the first word of the longest phrase the claim shares with its source (three or more words) and carry it through the citation chip; in the excerpt, mark only that shared phrase. With no shared phrase, mark the whole claim.
**Do** keep text on an ink in Ink (#1b1d21), and tint a chip that sits on its own ink with 10% Ink instead of repeating the colour.
**Do** separate regions with 1px hairlines and tone (White Ground against Library Grey), not with extra cards or shadows.
**Do** set text quoted from a document in Source Serif 4 and everything else in Source Sans 3, with tabular numerals.
**Do** confirm destructive actions inline in the row they affect (Remove / Keep) and return focus to the trigger when the person keeps the item.
**Do** keep the highlight swipe as the only authored motion, and stop every animation and transition under reduced motion.
**Do** put questions first at ≤820px: top bar, thread, sticky composer, then the library.
donts: **Don't** use a highlighter ink for status, hover, selection, buttons or decoration; the only non-evidence yellow is the highlighter drawn in the logo and in the searching bar.
**Don't** render answers as chat bubbles or switch to a dark chat template; an answer is document text under its question.
**Don't** dress the app in a theme (textures, rulers, motif strips, costume colours); the earlier Survey Sheet world was rejected for exactly that.
**Don't** add a second solid accent button: the Ask button is the only blue fill, and red fills only the inline Remove confirmation.
**Don't** give controls or cards the irregular swipe or highlight radius, or give chips a regular one.
**Don't** add shadows beyond the composer lift, the toast float and the 1px button contact shadow.
**Don't** introduce a display size above the 23px question heading.
